title: REQ-20261113-OPS005 — Death benefit notification & supporting documents: Mei Chen, Caldova Pension CP-3019042 (claimants Robert & Lily Chen)
content:
Death notification received by email on 13 Nov 2026 from Robert Chen (DOB 30/01/1974, age 52; Box Hill VIC; robert.chen@example.com; 0491 570 006), acting for himself and his sister Lily Chen (DOB 11/05/1977, age 49). Their mother, Mei Chen (DOB 05/06/1945), died on 12 Oct 2026, aged 81. Robert is quiet and organised for the family: 'Mum always said she'd sorted everything — I just want to do this right for her.'

Member account: Caldova Pension CP-3019042, balance $486,200 on 13 Nov 2026, before any redemption. Adviser: Marcus Tan (adviser code ADV-20871), Bayside Financial Partners, Brighton — copied on Robert's email. The pension was paid quarterly; the last payment was on 15 Sep 2026, so no payment fell due between the date of death and the notification. Pension payments are stopped on notification and the 15 Dec 2026 payment is cancelled. There is no reversionary beneficiary — Mei's husband predeceased her.

Nomination on file: binding death benefit nomination signed 18 Mar 2024 — Robert 50%, Lily 50% — lapsing, valid to 18 Mar 2027, so in force at the date of death.

Documents received: certified copy of the death certificate (Victorian Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages); a death benefit claim form from each of Robert and Lily; certified ID — Robert: Victorian driver licence; Lily: Australian passport (specimens — demo only); bank account details for each claimant in their own name; a statement from each that they were not financially dependent on Mei and not in an interdependency relationship with her. Probate is not needed while a valid binding nomination directs payment to the nominees.

Case set-up: REQ-20261113-OPS005 opened (request type: Death benefit claim). Case owner: Client Operations Team Leader (compassionate oversight). Bereavement handling: one point of contact, email preferred by Robert, no marketing or surveys, gentle plain-English language, and never ask the family for the same document twice.

Routing: Financial Crime (authenticity of the death certificate and claimant IDs) → Benefits & Eligibility (BDBN validity, SIS dependants, tax dependency) → Investment Solutions (redeem the pension portfolio to cash; final amounts depend on sale proceeds) → Payments (per-beneficiary components and tax; Team Leader approval in Microsoft Teams — any death benefit) → Client Communications (condolence letters to Robert and Lily with a plain-English tax explanation, timeline and complaint rights).
